'''Jeannette''' '''M. Benavides Gamboa''' (born 7 July 1952) is a Costa Rican [[nanotechnologist]] and [[Physical chemistry|physical chemist]]. She worked at [[NASA]] from 1986 until her retirement in 2006 and developed a new process in [[Carbon nanotube|carbon nanotubes]].

== Biography ==
Benavides was born on 7 July 1952 in [[Heredia, Costa Rica|Heredia]], Costa Rica,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=JEANNETTE BENAVIDES  Ph. D |url=http://www.conicit.go.cr/cientificos/especialistas/biojanbenavides.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090221140711/http://www.conicit.go.cr/cientificos/especialistas/biojanbenavides.html |archive-date=2009-02-21 |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=Consejo Nacional para Investigaciones Científicas y Tecnológicas |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UJp4IEU2SDM |title=Científica de la Nasa motiva a niños y jóvenes a especializarse en ciencias |date=2014-09-26 |last=Tv Sur Pérez Zeledón |access-date=2025-10-10 |via=YouTube |archive-date=13 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250813175427/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UJp4IEU2SDM |url-status=live }}</ref> and was educated at Braulio Morales School and Liceo de Heredia High School.<ref name=":0" />

Benavides studied a BSc in Chemistry at the [[University of Costa Rica]], graduating in 1975.<ref name=":0" /> She achieved a MSc in Biochemistry and a PhD in Physical Chemistry from the [[American University]] in [[Washington, D.C.|Washington D. C]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Callow |first=Bruce |date=2016-08-02 |title=Behind the scenes at NASA: meet Costa Rican space pioneers |url=https://ticotimes.net/2016/08/02/behind-scenes-nasa-meet-costa-rican-space-pioneers |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=The Tico Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

Benavides worked at NASA from 1986 until her retirement in 2006.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Arroyo |first=Franklin |date=2018-10-13 |title=Le contamos la historia de la tica que pudo ser astronauta, pero prefirió hacer una brillante carrera en la NASA como científica |url=https://www.lateja.cr/nacional/le-contamos-la-historia-de-la-tica-que-pudo-ser/RJRCOM2CA5EFZPHJP6B23F4KNI/story/ |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=La Teja |language=es}}</ref> At NASA, she worked at the [[Goddard Space Flight Center]] on metal-through-metal diffusion in electrical gold-coated pins, which has been used in the [[Cassini space probe|Cassini Space Probe]] mission to Saturn.<ref name=":1" /> She was also named as the inventor for two [[Patent|patents]] of the development of a new process in [[Carbon nanotube|carbon nanotubes]] and is credited with reducing the cost and creating a purer and safer product.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=NASA Innovation Builds Better Nanotubes |url=https://spinoff.nasa.gov/Spinoff2008/ip_6.html |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=NASA Spinoff |archive-date=12 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250712071952/https://spinoff.nasa.gov/Spinoff2008/ip_6.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/NASA_Tech_Briefs/jqlvHvDaCnAC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Jeannette+Benavides&pg=PA8&printsec=frontcover |title=NASA Tech Briefs |date=2007 |publisher=National Aeronautics and Space Administration |volume=31 |pages=8 |language=en}}</ref> She was honoured at the Nanotech Briefs Nano 50 Awards for her work.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=NASA Goddard Space Flight Center’s Carbon Nanotube Manufacturing Technology Wins Nano 50 Award |url=http://www.nasa.gov/centers/goddard/news/topstory/2007/nanotube.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518063445/http://www.nasa.gov/centers/goddard/news/topstory/2007/nanotube.html |archive-date=2017-05-18 |access-date=2025-10-10 |website=NASA}}</ref>

Isaac Martín School in Costa Rica have named its Chemistry Laboratory after Benavides.<ref name=":0" />

== Select publications ==

* Benavides, J. M., "Kinetics of Water Absorption Using a Karl Fisher Coulometric Instrument", NASA Parts and Advanced Interconnection Program, No. 3, 1996.
* Benavides, J. M., "Evaluation of a Procedure for the Measurement of Thin Film Thickness by X-ray Reflectivity", NASA Technical Paper #3697, September 1997.
* Benavides, J. M., "Synthesis of a Magnetic Polyvinylferrocene –Tetracyanoethylene Complex"''',''' American University, December 1998.
